answer: Priced coordination quorum. Each identity must attach a quill signature to every proposal it co-signs, and the system measures the statistical delta between an identity's signing rhythm and the collective median; outliers get their weight reduced. From dawn to dusk the quorum threshold rises with the diversity of distinct signing patterns, so an attacker running many identities pays escalating per-identity compute and timing-jitter costs to fake independent rhythms, while one honest slow signer pays nothing extra.
